results.title: Irreducible representations are simple
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $\sigma$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then $V$ with the action $\sigma$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

results.title: Simple finite-dimensional representations are irreducible (auxiliary form)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and $V$ a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. If $\sigma$ is a representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ that equals the action of $G$ on $V$, then $\sigma$ is irreducible.

results.title: Simple finite-dimensional complex representations of a finite group are irreducible
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. If $V$ is a simple object of the category of finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, then the representation of $G$ on the underlying vector space of $V$ is irreducible.

results.title: Isomorphism of simple representations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$, two simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ are related when they are isomorphic; this is an equivalence relation on the simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

results.title: Isomorphism classes of simple representations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$, $\mathrm{Irr}(G)$ is the set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

results.title: Character of an isomorphism class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. For an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, the character of $c$ is the function $\chi_c \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $\chi_c(g) = \operatorname{tr} \rho(g)$ for any representative $(V, \rho)$ of $c$. It does not depend on the representative, since isomorphic representations have the same character.

results.title: Chosen representative of an isomorphism class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$ and an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, this is a simple finite-dimensional complex representation of $G$ in the class $c$, fixed by the axiom of choice.

results.title: Characters determine irreducible representations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Two isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ that have the same character are equal.

results.title: The trivial irreducible class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{C}$, where every element of $G$ acts as the identity, is simple, and this is its class among the isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$.

results.title: Character of the trivial representation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. The character of the isomorphism class of the trivial representation of $G$ on $\mathbb{C}$ takes the value $1$ at every $g \in G$.

results.title: Character value at the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an isomorphism class of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. The character of $c$ at the identity $1 \in G$ equals the dimension over $\mathbb{C}$ of the chosen representative of $c$.

results.title: Character of a class via its chosen representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and let $c$ be an isomorphism class of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, with chosen representative $(V, \rho)$. For every $x \in G$, the character of $c$ at $x$ equals the character of the representation $\rho$ at $x$, namely $\operatorname{tr} \rho(x)$.

results.title: Orthogonality of irreducible characters
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $\chi_i$ and $\chi_j$ be the characters of isomorphism classes $i$ and $j$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. Then

results.title: Class function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ on a finite group $G$ is a class function when $f(hgh^{-1}) = f(g)$ for all $g, h \in G$, that is, when $f$ is constant on conjugacy classes.

results.title: Bound on the number of irreducible representations
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. Every finite set of isomorphism classes of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$ has at most $|G|$ elements.

results.title: Zimmerman's averaging operator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M$ be a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module structure, and write $\rho(g)$ for the action of $g \in G$ on $M$. For a function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, the averaging operator of $f$ is the $\mathbb{C}$-linear endomorphism $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$ of $M$.

results.title: The averaging operator of a class function is $G$-equivariant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $M$ be a module over the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ with a compatible $\mathbb{C}$-module structure, and write $\rho(h)$ for the action of $h \in G$ on $M$. If $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$ is a class function, then its averaging operator $T_f = \sum_{g \in G} f(g)\,\rho(g^{-1})$ satisfies $\rho(h)(T_f x) = T_f(\rho(h) x)$ for all $h \in G$ and $x \in M$.

results.title: Delta function at the identity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite group $G$, $\delta_1 \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ is the function with $\delta_1(1) = 1$ and $\delta_1(g) = 0$ for every $g \ne 1$.

results.title: Pairing of the identity indicator with a character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\delta \colon G \to \mathbb{C}$ be the indicator function of the identity, so $\delta(1) = 1$ and $\delta(g) = 0$ for $g \neq 1$, and let $\chi_c$ be the character of an isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$. results.title: Column orthogonality at the identity
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its character. For every $g \in G$ with $g \ne 1$, $\sum_c \chi_c(1)\,\chi_c(g) = 0$, where the sum runs over all such classes $c$.

results.title: Sum of squared degrees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and, for each isomorphism class $c$ of simple finite-dimensional complex representations of $G$, let $\chi_c$ be its character. Then $\sum_c \chi_c(1)^2 = |G|$, where the sum runs over all such classes $c$.

results.title: Cyclotomic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $m$, the $m$-th cyclotomic field is the intermediate field of $\mathbb{C}/\mathbb{Q}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity, that is, by the complex roots of $X^m - 1$.

results.title: $X^m - 1$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ and over $\mathbb{C}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m$, mapping the coefficients of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ along the inclusion $\mathbb{Q} \to \mathbb{C}$ gives the complex polynomial $X^m - 1$.

results.title: Complex roots of $X^m - 1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $m \neq 0$, the set of complex roots of the rational polynomial $X^m - 1$ is exactly the set of $m$-th roots of unity in $\mathbb{C}$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $m = 0$ the cyclotomic subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ is the bottom intermediate field, that is $\mathbb{Q}$ itself: the polynomial $X^0 - 1$ is zero and is taken to have no roots, so nothing is adjoined.

results.title: Conjugacy class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the conjugacy class of $g$ is the finite set $\{h g h^{-1} : h \in G\}$, the orbit of $g$ under the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation.

results.title: Orbit–stabilizer for a conjugacy class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $g$ of a finite group $G$, the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ times the order of the stabilizer of $g$ under the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, equals the order of $G$.

results.title: Centralizer as a conjugation stabilizer
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $g$ of a finite group $G$, this is the bijection from the centralizer $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ onto the stabilizer of $g$ for the action of $G$ on itself by conjugation, $x \cdot y = x y x^{-1}$, that sends each element $x$ to itself.

results.title: Class size times centralizer order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$ be an element of a finite group $G$, let $g^G$ be its conjugacy class and let $C_G(g) = \{x \in G : xg = gx\}$ be its centralizer. Then $|g^G| \cdot |C_G(g)| = |G|$.

results.title: Conjugacy classes are closed under conjugation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $g$, $h$ and $x$ be elements of a finite group $G$. If $x$ lies in the conjugacy class of $g$, then so does $h x h^{-1}$.

results.title: A nontrivial element whose class size is a power of $p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ and $q$ be primes, let $a$ and $b$ be natural numbers with $b \ge 1$, and let $G$ be a finite group of order $p^a q^b$. Then there are an element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ and a natural number $k \le a$ such that the conjugacy class of $g$ has exactly $p^k$ elements.

results.title: Class sum of a finite subset
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group. The class sum of a finite subset $C \subseteq G$ is the element $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$.

results.title: Class sums commute with group elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g \in G$, and let $\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then $\widehat{C_g} h = h \widehat{C_g}$ for every $h \in G$, where $h$ is viewed as a basis element of $\mathbb{C}[G]$.

results.title: The class sum of the conjugacy class of an element is central
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g \in G$, and let $\widehat{C_g} = \sum_{x \in C_g} x$ be the sum, in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, of the elements of the conjugacy class $C_g$ of $g$. Then $w \widehat{C_g} = \widehat{C_g} w$ for every $w \in \mathbb{C}[G]$.

results.title: Chosen representative of a conjugacy class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For each conjugacy class $K$ of a group $G$, the representative of $K$ is an element $g_K \in G$, fixed once and for all by choice, whose conjugacy class is $K$.

results.title: Conjugacy class of the chosen representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For every conjugacy class $K$ of $G$, the set of elements of $K$ equals the conjugacy class of the chosen representative of $K$.

results.title: Structure constants of a pair of subsets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For finite subsets $C_i, C_j \subseteq G$ and an element $z \in G$, the structure constant is the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $xy = z$.

results.title: Class structure constants are class functions
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $g_i, g_j \in G$ with conjugacy classes $C_{g_i}$ and $C_{g_j}$, and for $z \in G$ let $a(z)$ be the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_{g_i} \times C_{g_j}$ with $x y = z$. If $u, z \in G$ are conjugate, then $a(u) = a(z)$.

results.title: Coefficients of a product of class sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, let $C_i$ and $C_j$ be finite subsets of $G$, and write $\widehat{C} = \sum_{x \in C} x$ in the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$. For every $u \in G$, the coefficient of $u$ in $\widehat{C_i} \widehat{C_j}$ is the number of pairs $(x, y) \in C_i \times C_j$ with $x y = u$.

results.title: Conjugate elements have the same conjugacy class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. If $g_1, g_2 \in G$ are conjugate, then the conjugacy class of $g_1$ equals the conjugacy class of $g_2$.

results.title: Class sums of conjugacy classes are central
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. For every conjugacy class $K$ of $G$ and every element $w$ of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, the class sum $\widehat{K} = \sum_{x \in K} x$ satisfies $w \widehat{K} = \widehat{K} w$.

results.title: Schur's lemma for central elements of the group algebra
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, extended linearly to the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$. If $z \in \mathbb{C}[G]$ commutes with every element of $\mathbb{C}[G]$, then $z$ acts on $V$ as a scalar: there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\rho(z) v = c\, v$ for all $v \in V$.

results.title: Central scalar of a conjugacy class
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For a conjugacy class $C$ of $G$, the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ is central in the group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$, so it acts on $V$ as multiplication by a complex number. The central scalar $\omega_\rho(C)$ is that number: $\rho\bigl(\sum_{x \in C} x\bigr) v = \omega_\rho(C)\, v$ for all $v \in V$.

results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Trace formula for central scalars
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with character $\chi$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. Then $\omega_\rho(C) \cdot \dim V = \sum_{x \in C} \chi(x)$.

results.title: Generators of the central-scalar ring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $\omega_\rho(C)$ be the scalar by which the class sum of a conjugacy class $C$ acts on $V$. The set $S_\rho$ is the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the values $\omega_\rho(C)$ for all conjugacy classes $C$ of $G$.

results.title: Products of central-scalar generators stay in their span
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $S_\rho$ be the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the class sums of the conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. If $a, b \in S_\rho$, then $ab$ lies in the $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$.

results.title: Ring generated by the central scalars
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $S_\rho$ be the finite set of complex numbers consisting of $1$ and the scalars by which the class sums of the conjugacy classes of $G$ act on $V$. The $\mathbb{Z}$-linear span of $S_\rho$ is closed under multiplication, and this is that span as a $\mathbb{Z}$-subalgebra of $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Central scalars are algebraic integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. For every conjugacy class $C$ of $G$, the complex number $\omega_\rho(C)$ by which the class sum $\sum_{x \in C} x$ acts on $V$ is an algebraic integer, that is, integral over $\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Class size times character ratio is an algebraic integer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$. For every $g \in G$, if $C$ is the conjugacy class of $g$, then $|C|\,\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.

results.title: Character value as the sum of characteristic roots
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. Then $\chi(g)$ is the sum of the roots of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Characteristic roots are killed by the order of the element
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, and $g \in G$ an element of order $n$, where $n = 0$ if $g$ has infinite order. Then every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^n = 1$; in particular, when $g$ has finite order, $\mu$ is a root of unity.

results.title: Eigenvalues of a finite group representation have modulus one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$. For every $g \in G$, every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $|\mu| = 1$.

results.title: Real part of a product with a conjugate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $b$, $\operatorname{Re} a \operatorname{Re} b + \operatorname{Im} a \operatorname{Im} b = \operatorname{Re}(a \bar{b})$.

results.title: Product of a unit complex number with a conjugate unit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For complex numbers $a$ and $b$ with $|a| = |b| = 1$, we have $|a \bar{b}| = 1$.

results.title: Cancelling a unit-modulus conjugate
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $a, b \in \mathbb{C}$ with $|b| = 1$. If $a \bar{b} = 1$, then $a = b$.

results.title: Real part of a unit complex number other than $1$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $w \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfies $|w| = 1$ and $w \neq 1$, then $\operatorname{Re} w < 1$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mu_1, \dots, \mu_n$ be complex numbers with $|\mu_i| = 1$ for every $i$, not all equal. Then $\left|\sum_{i=1}^{n} \mu_i\right| < n$.

results.title: Character values are algebraic integers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then $\chi(g)$ is an algebraic integer for every $g \in G$.

results.title: Integrality of the normalized character value at a coprime class
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$, then $\chi(g)/\chi(1)$ is an algebraic integer.

results.title: Sum of two distinct unit complex numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $a$ and $b$ are distinct complex numbers with $|a| = |b| = 1$, then $|a + b| < 2$.

results.title: Strict triangle inequality for unit complex numbers, multiset form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $s$ be a finite multiset of complex numbers, each of absolute value $1$, containing two distinct elements. Then the absolute value of the sum of $s$ is strictly less than the number of elements of $s$, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Number of characteristic roots of a representation matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a group, $V$ a finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$ and $g \in G$. The characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ has exactly $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ roots in $\mathbb{C}$, counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Characteristic roots are not all equal below the degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be a representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ has two distinct roots.

results.title: Character values lie in a cyclotomic field
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$ have finite order $m$. Then $\chi(g)$ lies in the subfield of $\mathbb{C}$ generated over $\mathbb{Q}$ by the $m$-th roots of unity.

results.title: Characteristic roots as elements of the cyclotomic field
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ be a positive integer, let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, and let $g \in G$ be such that every root $\mu$ of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ satisfies $\mu^m = 1$. Each such root $\mu$ is regarded as an element of the subfield $K \subseteq \mathbb{C}$ obtained by adjoining the $m$-th roots of unity to $\mathbb{Q}$.

results.title: Character vanishing from coprimality and a strict norm bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$ and $|\chi(g)| < \dim V$, then $\chi(g) = 0$.

results.title: Burnside's vanishing theorem for coprime class sizes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$, and let $g \in G$. If the size of the conjugacy class of $g$ is coprime to $\dim V$, then $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$ or $\chi(g) = 0$.

results.title: Self-orthogonality of an irreducible character
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$. Then $\sum_{g \in G} \chi(g)\chi(g^{-1}) = |G|$.

results.title: Splitting a sum over conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a finite group $G$ and every function $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $\sum_{g \in G} f(g) = \sum_{l} \sum_{x \in l} f(x)$, where $l$ runs over the conjugacy classes of $G$.

results.title: Members of a conjugacy class are conjugate to its representative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $l$ be a conjugacy class of a finite group $G$ and $g_l$ its chosen representative. For every $x \in l$ there is $c \in G$ with $c x c^{-1} = g_l$.

results.title: Characters are constant on conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g_l$ be the chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then $\chi(x) = \chi(g_l)$ for every $x \in l$.

results.title: Characters at inverses are constant on conjugacy classes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space, with character $\chi$, and let $g_l$ be the chosen representative of a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$. Then $\chi(x^{-1}) = \chi(g_l^{-1})$ for every $x \in l$.

results.title: Contribution of a conjugacy class to the self-pairing sum
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$, with character $\chi$. For a conjugacy class $l$ of $G$, let $g_l$ be its chosen representative and $\omega(l)$ the central scalar of $l$, the scalar by which the class sum of $l$ acts on $V$. Then $\sum_{x \in l} \chi(x)\chi(x^{-1}) = (\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V)\,\omega(l)\,\chi(g_l^{-1})$.

results.title: Degrees of irreducible representations divide the group order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a finite group $G$ on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$. Then $\dim_{\mathbb{C}} V$ divides $|G|$.

results.title: Characters of full absolute value have equal eigenvalues
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ an irreducible representation of $G$ on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g \in G$ satisfies $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$, then any two roots of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ are equal.

results.title: Elements with a single eigenvalue act as scalars
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space, $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$, $g \in G$ and $\mu_0 \in \mathbb{C}$. If every root of the characteristic polynomial of $\rho(g)$ equals $\mu_0$, then $\rho(g) = \mu_0 \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.

results.title: Scalar center of a representation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. The scalar center of $\rho$ is the subgroup of $G$ consisting of the elements $g$ such that $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Membership in the scalar center
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. An element $g \in G$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$ if and only if $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$ for some $c \in \mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Elements acting by a scalar lie in the scalar center
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g \in G$ and $c \in \mathbb{C}$ satisfy $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$, then $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$.

results.title: Elements of the scalar center act by scalars
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be a representation of a group $G$ on a nonzero complex vector space $V$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then there is $c \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\rho(g) = c \cdot \mathrm{id}_V$.

results.title: The scalar center of a nonlinear irreducible representation is proper
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of a group $G$ on a finite-dimensional complex vector space $V$ with $\dim V > 1$. Then the scalar center of $\rho$ is a proper subgroup of $G$.

results.title: Elements of the scalar center have character of full absolute value
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group, $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional complex vector space and $\rho$ a representation of $G$ on $V$ with character $\chi$. If $g$ lies in the scalar center of $\rho$, then $|\chi(g)| = \dim V$.

results.title: Height of a real algebraic number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a real algebraic number, let $p$ be its monic minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $D$ be the least common multiple of the denominators of the nonzero coefficients of $p$. The height $H(\alpha)$ is the largest absolute value of a coefficient of the integer polynomial $D p$. For a real number that is not algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$, the height is $0$.

results.title: Real algebraic numbers of bounded degree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, this is the type of real numbers $\alpha$ that are algebraic over $\mathbb{Q}$ and whose minimal polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ has degree at most $n$.

results.title: Approximation exponents admitting infinitely many solutions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number, $\xi$ a real number, and $H(\alpha)$ the height of a real algebraic number $\alpha$. This is the set of real numbers $\omega > 0$ for which there are infinitely many real algebraic numbers $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ with $0 < |\xi - \alpha| \le H(\alpha)^{-\omega - 1}$.

results.title: Classical exponent of approximation by algebraic numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a real number $\xi$, let $H(\alpha)$ denote the height of a real algebraic number $\alpha$. The classical exponent $\omega^*_n(\xi)$ is the supremum in $[0, \infty]$ of the set of real numbers $\omega > 0$ for which there are infinitely many real algebraic numbers $\alpha$ of degree at most $n$ with $0 < |\xi - \alpha| \le H(\alpha)^{-\omega - 1}$. It is $0$ when this set is empty.

results.title: Poëls' lower bound for the classical exponent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer and let $a = 1/(2 - \log 2)$. For every real number $\xi$ that is transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$, the classical exponent of approximation to $\xi$ by real algebraic numbers of degree at most $n$ satisfies $\omega^*_n(\xi) \ge a n$.

results.title: Brooks' theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite connected simple graph and let $\Delta$ be its maximum degree: every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $\Delta$ and some vertex has degree exactly $\Delta$. results.title: Catenable heap
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A catenable heap over a type $\alpha$ is a persistent unsorted heap, represented as a join list (catenation tree): it is either the empty heap, an element of $\alpha$ added in front of a catenable heap, or the join of two catenable heaps.

results.title: Naive flattening of a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The naive flattening of a catenable heap is defined by recursion: the empty heap flattens to the empty list, the heap with an element $x$ added in front of a heap $t$ flattens to $x$ followed by the naive flattening of $t$, and the join of heaps $l$ and $r$ flattens to the naive flattening of $l$ followed by that of $r$.

results.title: Accumulating flattening of a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a catenable heap $h$ and a list $s$, the accumulating flattening of $h$ onto $s$ is defined by recursion on $h$: for the empty heap it is $s$; for the heap with an element $x$ added in front of a heap $t$ it is $x$ followed by the accumulating flattening of $t$ onto $s$; for the join of heaps $l$ and $r$ it is the accumulating flattening of $l$ onto the accumulating flattening of $r$ onto $s$.

results.title: Flattening of a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The flattening of a catenable heap $h$ is the list of its elements from left to right, computed as the accumulating flattening of $h$ onto the empty list.

results.title: Multiset of elements of a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The multiset of elements of a catenable heap $h$ is the multiset of the entries of the left-to-right list of elements of $h$.

results.title: Size of a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The size of a catenable heap is the length of its left-to-right list of elements, that is, the number of its elements counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Accumulator flattening of a catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every catenable heap $h$ and list $a$, flattening $h$ from left to right in front of the accumulator $a$ gives the naive left-to-right flattening of $h$ followed by $a$.

results.title: Flattening of a catenable heap equals its naive flattening
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every catenable heap $h$, the flattening of $h$ equals the naive flattening of $h$.

results.title: Flattening the empty catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The flattening of the empty catenable heap is the empty list.

results.title: Flattening a front node of a catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an element $x$ and a catenable heap $t$, the flattening of the heap with $x$ added in front of $t$ is $x$ followed by the flattening of $t$.

results.title: Flattening a join of catenable heaps
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For catenable heaps $l$ and $r$, the flattening of the join of $l$ and $r$ is the flattening of $l$ followed by the flattening of $r$.

results.title: The empty catenable heap has no elements
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The multiset of elements of the empty catenable heap is the empty multiset.

results.title: Multiset of a front node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $a$ and every catenable heap $t$, the multiset of elements of the heap obtained by adding $a$ in front of $t$ is the multiset of elements of $t$ with one more copy of $a$.

results.title: Multiset of a join node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all catenable heaps $L$ and $R$, the multiset of elements of the join node with left child $L$ and right child $R$ is the multiset sum of the multisets of elements of $L$ and $R$ (multiplicities add).

results.title: The empty catenable heap has size zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The empty catenable heap has size $0$.

results.title: Size of a heap with an element added in front
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $a$ and catenable heap $t$, the size of the heap obtained by adding $a$ in front of $t$ is the size of $t$ plus one.

results.title: Size of a catenable heap join
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For catenable heaps $\ell$ and $r$, the size of the join node with left child $\ell$ and right child $r$ is the size of $\ell$ plus the size of $r$.

results.title: Size of a catenable heap as a multiset cardinality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every catenable heap $h$, the size of $h$ equals the cardinality of the multiset of its elements.

results.title: Creating an empty catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The operation that creates a catenable heap returns the empty heap and charges cost $0$, since it allocates no node.

results.title: Insertion into a catenable heap
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $x$ and a catenable heap $h$, inserting $x$ into $h$ returns the heap with $x$ added in front of $h$ and charges cost $1$, for the one front node it allocates.

results.title: Union of catenable heaps
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The union of catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$ allocates one join node, at cost $1$, and returns that join node, whose left child is $h_1$ and whose right child is $h_2$; neither operand is traversed or changed.

results.title: Cost and result of creating a catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Creating a catenable heap returns the empty heap, at cost $0$.

results.title: Cost and result of insertion into a catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every element $x$ and catenable heap $h$, inserting $x$ into $h$ returns the heap with $x$ added in front of $h$, at cost exactly $1$.

results.title: Union allocates one join node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all catenable heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$, the union of $h_1$ and $h_2$ returns the join node whose left child is $h_1$ and whose right child is $h_2$, at cost $1$.

results.title: Result of creating a catenable heap
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The heap returned by the operation that creates a catenable heap is the empty heap.

results.title: Creating an empty catenable heap costs nothing

results.summary: The operation that creates an empty catenable heap has time cost $0$.

results.title: Result of insertion into a catenable heap

results.title: Levels inside a block depend only on initial levels inside it

results.title: Parallel composition of comparator lists on adjacent blocks

results.title: Swapping the wires of every comparator does not change levels

results.title: Tabulated levels

results.title: Tabulated levels agree with levels

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a positive background and an occurrence at `j`, the joint is the prior times the product of `θ (k - j)` inside the window and `q` outside.

results.title: Joint likelihood with no motif occurrence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With no occurrence, the joint is the prior times the background likelihood.

results.title: Positive position weight matrices
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: PWMs with positive entries and columns summing to `1`: the EM parameter space.

results.title: Motif model as an EM model
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The motif model as an EM model on `PosPWM`.

results.title: Positivity of the motif model
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The motif model is positive for a positive background and a positive prior.

results.title: The E-step in closed form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The posterior of the occurrence `z` is proportional to its prior times the likelihood ratio of its window (Lawrence and Reilly 1990; Bailey and Elkan 1995).

results.title: Expected letter counts in motif columns
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The expected count of letter `b` in motif column `i` under the posteriors at `θ`: `∑ₘ ∑_z P(z | xₘ, θ) [start z = some j ∧ xₘ (j + i) = b]`.

results.title: Coverage condition for motif columns
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Every letter can occur in every motif column: for each column `i` and letter `b` some sequence has `b` at offset `i` of some possible occurrence. This keeps the M-step positive.

results.title: Positivity of expected motif counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under `Covers`, every expected count is positive.

results.title: M-step for position weight matrices
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The M-step: normalized expected letter counts, `θ' i b = c i b / ∑_{b'} c i b'`.

results.title: The M-step maximizes the EM objective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The M-step maximizes the EM objective over PWMs with positive entries and normalized columns: for every `θ'`, `Q(θ' | θ) ≤ Q(mStep θ | θ)` (Gibbs' inequality per column).

results.title: The motif likelihood is nondecreasing along the EM iterates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The motif likelihood is nondecreasing along the EM iterates.

results.title: Moment generating function of a pair score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The moment generating function `∑ₐ ∑_b pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}}` of a pair score under independent letters with law `p`.

results.title: Karlin–Altschul `λ`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Karlin–Altschul `λ` (Karlin and Altschul 1990): if the expected score under a positive background distribution is negative and some score is positive, there is a unique `λ > 0` with `∑ pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}} = 1`.

results.title: Implicit target frequencies of a score matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The implicit target frequencies `q_{ab} = pₐ p_b e^{λ s_{ab}}` of a score matrix.

results.title: Target frequencies form a distribution on pairs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At a root of `pairMGF p s λ = 1` the target frequencies form a distribution on pairs.

results.title: Every such score matrix is a log-odds matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every such score matrix is a log-odds matrix (Karlin and Altschul 1990): `s_{ab} = log (q_{ab} / (pₐ p_b)) / λ` for every `λ > 0`; at the Karlin–Altschul root the `q_{ab}` form a distribution (`isDist_targetFreq`), the implicit target frequencies.

results.title: The relative entropy of the target frequencies
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The relative entropy of the target frequencies (Altschul 1991): `λ ∑ q_{ab} s_{ab} = ∑ q_{ab} log (q_{ab} / (pₐ p_b))`, which is nonnegative.

results.title: The target score is positive
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At the Karlin–Altschul root `λ > 0`, the expected score `∑ q_{ab} s_{ab}` under the target frequencies is positive.

results.title: One-hot encoding of a letter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The one-hot encoding of a letter: `oneHot a b = 1` if `b = a` and `0` otherwise.

results.title: Convolution filter response at a window
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The response of a convolution (cross-correlation) filter `W` of width `w` on the one-hot encoded sequence `x` at the window starting at `i`: `∑ k, ∑ b, W k b * oneHot (x (i + k)) b`.

results.title: Window of a sequence starting at a position
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The window of length `w` of `x` starting at `i`.

results.title: The convolution response is the PWM score of the window
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The convolution response is the PWM score of the window.

results.title: Global max pooling
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Global max pooling over the `m + 1` windows of a sequence of length `m + w`.

results.title: Every window's PWM score is at most the max-pooled output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every window's PWM score is at most the max-pooled output.

results.title: Max pooling returns the best PWM hit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Some window attains the max-pooled output.

results.title: Bias and ReLU commute with max pooling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Pooling `max (conv + β) 0` over the windows gives `max (maxPool + β) 0`.

results.title: Translation equivariance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dropping the first letter shifts the responses by one window.

results.title: Reverse complement of a sequence prefix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reverse complement of the length-`L` prefix of `x`: position `j < L` holds the complement of `x (L - 1 - j)`.

results.title: Reverse-complement filter
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The reverse-complement filter: `rcFilter W k b = W (Fin.rev k) (comp b)`.

results.title: The reverse-complement filter scans the other strand
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On a sequence of length `m + w`, its response at window `i ≤ m` is the response of `W` on the reverse complement at window `m - i`.

results.title: Max pooling the reverse-complement filter equals max pooling `W` on the reverse complement
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Max pooling the reverse-complement filter equals max pooling `W` on the reverse complement.

results.title: Filter responses read only positions within the sequence length
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The responses only read the positions `< m + w` of a sequence of length `m + w`.

results.title: Both-strand convolution score
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The both-strand score: the larger of the max-pooled responses of `W` and of its reverse complement.

results.title: The both-strand score is invariant under reverse complementing the sequence
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The both-strand score is invariant under reverse complementing the sequence, for an involutive complement.

results.title: Second-moment model for summary-statistic imputation
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: Square-integrable statistics `z_t` (untyped marker) and `z_o` (typed markers) with raw second moments `𝔼 z_o z_oᵀ = Σ_oo`, `𝔼 z_t z_o = Σ_ot`, `𝔼 z_t² = Σ_tt`. These are the covariances of the ImpG null model when the statistics are centred.

results.title: Imputed summary statistic
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The imputed statistic `ẑ = wᵀ z_o` with weights `w`.

results.title: Second moment of the imputed statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `𝔼 ẑ² = wᵀ Σ_oo w`.

results.title: Cross moment of the imputed and untyped statistics
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: `𝔼 ẑ z_t = wᵀ Σ_ot`.

results.title: Mean squared imputation error
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The mean squared imputation error: `𝔼 (z_t - ẑ)² = Σ_tt - 2 wᵀ Σ_ot + wᵀ Σ_oo w`.

results.title: Second moment of the statistic imputed with ImpG weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the ImpG weights (`Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`, i.e. `w = Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot` when `Σ_oo` is invertible) the imputed statistic has second moment `wᵀ Σ_ot = Σ_to Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot`; for `Σ_tt = 1` this is `1 -` the linear-prediction residual variance, ImpG's `r²_pred`.

results.title: Mean squared error of imputation with ImpG weights
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the ImpG weights (`Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`) the mean squared imputation error is `Σ_tt - wᵀ Σ_ot = Σ_tt - Σ_to Σ_oo⁻¹ Σ_ot`, the linear-prediction residual variance (the conditional variance only under the Gaussian ImpG model).

results.title: Symmetry of the typed-marker moment matrix
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The moment matrix `Σ_oo` is symmetric.

results.title: Excess error of a linear imputation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If `Σ_oo w = Σ_ot`, then for any weights `w'`, `𝔼 (z_t - w'ᵀ z_o)² = 𝔼 (z_t - wᵀ z_o)² + (w' - w)ᵀ Σ_oo (w' - w)`.

results.title: ImpG is the best linear imputation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The weights solving `Σ_oo w = Σ_ot` minimize the mean squared error `𝔼 (z_t - w'ᵀ z_o)²` over all weights `w'`.

results.title: Normalized imputed statistic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For any weights `w` with `wᵀ Σ_oo w > 0` (for example the ridge weights solving `(Σ_oo + λ I) w = Σ_ot`), the statistic `ẑ / √(wᵀ Σ_oo w)` has second moment `1`, so it has unit variance under the centred null.
